check_service_status.description: Check whether The Quotes Hub is answering, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can branch on it and fall back to a saved quote when the service is down. Being throttled is reported separately from being down. No API key required.
check_service_status.display_str_template: Check whether The Quotes Hub is up.

mock_response.message: The Quotes Hub is up and serving quotes.

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

message.description: What happened, in a sentence worth posting.

online.description: True when the service answered with a quote. This is the field to branch on.

rate_limited.description: True when the answer was a throttle (HTTP 429). Being throttled is not the same as being down.

reachable.description: True when something answered at all, even with an error. False means the request never landed.

response_time_ms.description: How long the request took, in milliseconds, or null when nothing came back.

status_code.description: The HTTP status that came back, or null when nothing did.

get_quote.description: Get one quotation by its number, with its author and tags. The way to fetch a quote again later once an earlier step or a saved row has its id. No API key required.

quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.text: The memory of everything is very soon overwhelmed in time.

get_quote.name: get_quote

parameters.description: The quote's number, as List quotes and Get a random quote report it in their id field and as it appears at the end of the quote's api_url. Quotes are numbered from 0.
parameters.name: quote_id

quote.description: One quotation, with who said it and what it is filed under.

api_url.description: The quote's own address on The Quotes Hub, e.g. https://thequoteshub.com/api/quotes/1.

author.description: The name of the person it is attributed to.

author_id.description: The author's id, which Get quotes by author takes: their name URL-encoded, with + for spaces, e.g. 'Marcus+Aurelius'.

id.description: The quote's number, from 0. Get a quote takes one of these.

tags.description: The tags the quote is filed under, as they were typed. Get quotes by tag takes them, trying the tag listing's spelling when the typed one misses.

get_random_quote.description: Get one quotation chosen at random, with who said it and the tags it is filed under. The step behind a quote of the day, a sign-off line for a newsletter or an opener for a message, with a different quote every run. Name a tag or an author to draw only from their quotes, such as a daily quote on leadership. No API key required.

quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.text: The memory of everything is very soon overwhelmed in time.

get_random_quote.name: get_random_quote

parameters.description: Optional. Draw only from the quotes filed under this tag. The tag, as List tags reports it in the tag_id field, such as 'wisdom'. The Quotes Hub matches tags exactly, so a tag that misses is tried again in lower case and with hyphens for spaces; a tag from a quote's own tags works too. Leave it and Author empty to draw from every quote.
parameters.name: tag_id

parameters.description: Optional. Draw only from this author's quotes. The author, as List authors reports it in the author_id field and as every quote carries it beside the author's name, such as 'Marcus+Aurelius'. The author's full name, spelled the way those steps spell it, works too. Give a tag or an author, not both.

description: Quotations from The Quotes Hub: a random quote for a daily message or a newsletter sign-off, the whole collection a page at a time, one quote by its number, and quotes gathered by tag or by author. Tags and authors come with their own listings and quote counts, so a workflow can pick a theme or a voice and pull from it. Every quote carries its author, its tags and a link to itself. No account or API key required.
